caption:
Polio left her unable to walk at 14. She couldn't go to school anymore - so she built a movement to teach others to read instead.

K. V. Rabiya, from Vellilakkadu in Kerala's Malappuram district, was struck by polio at age 14, leaving her wheelchair-bound and unable to continue regular schooling - she had to study from home. Rather than being limited by it, in June 1992 she launched a grassroots adult-literacy campaign in Tirurangadi as part of Kerala's State Literacy Campaign, teaching illiterate people of all ages to read and write. She founded a volunteer organization called 'Chalanam' - meaning 'motion' - which expanded into continuing education, health awareness and rehabilitation support for other physically disabled people. She survived a cancer diagnosis in 2002 and returned to her work. She received a national youth award in 1994 and the Padma Shri in 2022 for social work and passed away on May 4, 2025, mourned publicly across the country.
